notes: Summary: Stratos builds an in-IDE copilot for enterprise dev teams; primary ask is reproducible, rollable model/version pinning for code completion.

Key requirements: per-keystroke streaming, sub-50ms token latency in US-West, deterministic suggestion reproducibility for audits, pin model + tokenizer + runtime flags, traceability for every suggestion (model-id + kernel-hash + container), canary + automatic rollback on eval regression
POC scope: integrate hosted API into internal VSCode extension, run 2-week canary (5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%) with automated eval gates and functional unit tests against curated prompt set

Eval gates: baseline metrics from current model (precision@1 on code completion unit tests, compile-success rate, suggestion harmfulness score). Acceptable delta: precision@1 drop <= 0.5% and compile failures increase <= 0.1% otherwise block rollout.

Rollout plan: canary 5% for 48h + daily evaluation; if pass -> 25% for 72h; if pass -> 100% in staged waves. Auto-rollback trigger: regressions above thresholds or latency SLO breach >10% for two consecutive hours.
Pinning needs: ability to pin exact model artifact (model-id + commit hash), quantization profile, kernel selection, and runtime config. Need immutable artifact reference in logs for compliance.
Reproducibility ask: deterministic seeds or replay mode for offline reproduction of suggestions; ability to snapshot request+kv-cache state for parity tests across versions.
Latency: target median per-token < 30ms under dev-team traffic profile; 95th percentile token latency < 80ms. Must support streaming partial tokens to client to maintain typing feel.
Cost sensitivity: primary product is freemium for small teams but enterprise plan expects unit costs to be predictable; want Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization tradeoffs.

Security: require SSO/SAML, org-level audit logs for every request, encryption with customer-managed keys (KMS) and data residency for EU customers. Security team: "Please provide SOC2 and network diagram."
